title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon with H-prime semiprime walks and bucket matching

claims.statement: For uniform secret s in Z_r*, given T=[s]P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0 for i=1..n with n>=2^20: Cheon's d=2^20 reduction to z=s^d in the subgroup H of order m=(r-1)/2^20, solved by a baby-step/giant-step whose elements are products of two H-primes walked in increasing order, one batched incomplete affine addition per step, 192-bit parity y-key with the six mu6 candidates per match, records routed by three data-independent hops to 2^84 owner nodes and matched in a direct-mapped bucket table with a chained pool (baby side inserted in full before the giant side probes), each node capping its own comparisons at 1.01x the per-node mean and its slots at 64 records, candidate pairs capped at 2^44 (fail on exceeding), each candidate retaining its 192-bit key and copied to both generating nodes named by its chain ids, so recovery is one linear re-walk of each of its two chains by their own generating nodes (at most 4 matching steps per chain, the kept values of the giant chain sent to the baby chain's node, at most 96 scalar multiplications per candidate), then 20 square roots and a 2^11-scalar-multiplication root-of-unity search. Coverage constant K = 6N^2/m >= 0.4952. Heuristic success at least 0.390050 under H1-H3 (1 - e^-K = 0.390550 rounded down, less the failure terms and the 0.0005 coverage allowance of H1), claimed 0.3900. Total work W = 140419503413075181594833793762535146 reference units at C=2000, including lists, tables with walk overhead, the shared F_p inversion of every round of records, tables and re-walks, all records, routing with relay work, matching, candidate forwarding, recovery with the F_r inversions forming the six z, kept-value forwarding, status collection, node setup, Lemma 1 and output; log2 W = 116.7572267, the bound holds for every n >= 2^20. Peak memory 2^123.3242 bytes (exact itemised sum over all nodes at full allocation, asserted as an integer inequality), preprocessing at most 2^115.7603 units (included), no advice.

experiments.purpose: Mode ledger recomputes every size, cap, memory sum and the exact score from integers; mode ec runs Algorithm A end to end on a small j=0 curve (walks, bucket matching, key-retaining candidates, one linear re-walk per chain with duplicates processed in arrival order and the 4-step cap counted as a failure, six-candidate check, d-th root) and compares success, comparison counts, false and true matches and bucket occupancy with the model; mode census counts exactly, on toy primes built by the production rules, the set R of off-diagonal candidates, whose share |R|/m is exactly the probability that the uniform z is a candidate, and compares it with 1 - e^-K (any toy size and K via m_bits, k, K_per_10000, first_seed, primes; 'all' runs 8 primes at m in [2^21, 2^22) at K = 0.4952). Toy scale only, one process and no routing; it supports H1 and does not establish production cost or production success.
